name: Lazy, not biased: reasoning and belief in fake news
author: Human Not Found
description: Original study: Pennycook, G., & Rand, D. G. (2019). Lazy, not biased: Susceptibility to partisan fake news is better explained by lack of reasoning than by motivated reasoning. Cognition, 188, 39-50. In two studies, 3,446 Mechanical Turk workers took the Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) and rated the accuracy of real and fake political news headlines favouring Democrats or Republicans. Higher CRT scores went with lower belief in fake news and better discernment between real and fake, even for headlines that matched the participant's party. In this template ten US participants (five Democrats, five Republicans) answer four CRT-2 items (Thomson & Oppenheimer, 2016) and then rate twelve headlines on the original 4-point accuracy scale: three true and three false favouring each party. The headlines are new, written for this template, and shown as text rather than as Facebook posts; the CRT items are multiple choice, offering the intuitive and the correct answer. Item ids mark each headline as true or false and pro-Democrat or pro-Republican. Measures: truth discernment (mean rating of true minus false headlines) and CRT score (share correct), each also given per participant so they can be related to each other and to the participant's party. Participants are simulated: each is a Model participant, using the free test model until you choose a model, so the first runs only check the design; with the test model every participant takes the sample answer.
